purpose: A broader simulated battery of paraphrased questions and plausible hard distractors. Labels are authored expectations for testing, not independent ground truth or proof of semantic understanding.

cases.query: How do we choose a solution when fixing one problem shifts the burden onto a different community?

direct.title: Ethical Trade-offs When Repairing Harm
direct.text: Compare alternatives when remedies create competing harms. Identify who bears each burden, protect rights, listen to affected people, and explain the decision.

distractor.title: Community Belonging and Group Affiliation
distractor.text: Explore identity, authenticity, and how people maintain belonging while navigating group expectations.

cases.query: The people affected say the compensation doesn't make up for what they actually lost. What now?

direct.title: Restorative Justice and Meaningful Repair
direct.text: Meaningful repair starts by listening to harmed people, understanding actual losses, and revising restitution or redress when it fails to meet their needs.

distractor.title: Transparent Governance
distractor.text: Institutions document decisions, publish reasons, and report governance outcomes to the public.

cases.query: Everyone wants progress, but nobody agrees which proposal should be tried first. How can the group get unstuck?

direct.title: Collective Sense-making SOP: Decentralized Consensus
direct.text: Make each person's reasons visible, identify a shared outcome, compare proposals, and choose a small reversible action to test together.

distractor.title: General Governance Principles
distractor.text: Governance describes institutions, policies, and broad principles for public decision-making.

cases.query: A decision turned out badly in a way people had warned about. What should those responsible do?

direct.title: Accountability After Harmful Decisions
direct.text: Review evidence and warnings, acknowledge responsibility for foreseeable harm, explain what went wrong, hear affected people, and revise safeguards.

distractor.title: Ethical Trade-offs and Decision Criteria
distractor.text: Decision-makers weigh competing values, compare alternatives, and explain difficult choices when priorities conflict.

cases.query: How can a process be fair when some participants have much more influence than others?

direct.title: Power, Fairness, and Meaningful Participation
direct.text: Notice unequal power, protect the voice and rights of less powerful participants, create meaningful opportunities to contribute, and make decisions transparent.

distractor.title: Personal Productivity and Morning Routines
distractor.text: Build a daily routine, organize tasks, and maintain personal productivity habits.

cases.query: How can someone remain genuine while their community expects them to conform?

direct.title: Community Belonging and Group Affiliation
direct.text: Explore belonging, authenticity, identity, and tensions between personal integrity and group expectations.

distractor.title: Institutional Budget Forecasting
distractor.text: Estimate revenue, operating costs, and budget variances for the next financial year.

cases.query: What should an institution provide so people can understand and scrutinize how a decision was made?

direct.title: Accountability and Transparent Governance
direct.text: Document the evidence and reasoning behind decisions, publish explanations, and make review and accountability possible.

distractor.title: Restorative Justice and Meaningful Repair
distractor.text: Repair should address the actual losses experienced by people harmed and revise restitution or redress when needed.

cases.query: Before acting on behalf of a community, how should decision-makers handle the wishes and rights of the people affected?

direct.title: Rights, Consent, and Affected People
direct.text: Protect rights, seek meaningful consent where appropriate, listen to affected people, and explain how their input informs the decision.

distractor.title: General Governance Principles
distractor.text: Governance describes institutions, policies, and broad principles for public decision-making.

cases.query: We can't settle the whole disagreement today. Is there a small safe way to learn what works before committing?

direct.title: Collective Sense-making SOP: Decentralized Consensus
direct.text: Identify a shared outcome and test a small reversible action, then review what the group learns before making a larger commitment.

distractor.title: Community Belonging and Group Affiliation
distractor.text: Explore identity, authenticity, and how people maintain belonging while navigating group expectations.

cases.query: When every available option has a downside, how should leaders compare the choices?

direct.title: Ethical Trade-offs and Decision Criteria
direct.text: Compare alternatives, identify who bears the burdens, protect rights, listen to affected people, and explain the reasons for the choice.

distractor.title: Individual Identity and Authenticity
distractor.text: Explore personal authenticity, identity, belonging, and group affiliation.
